newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan to be officially appointed to U.N. top post.
newsitem.headline: Annan to be officially appointed to U.N. top post.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the Ghanaian head of U.N. peacekeeping, will be formally appointed on Tuesday as U.N. Secretary-General by the General Assembly, the last step before he begins his five-year term on January 1.

Mindful that Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, in his bid for a second term, was torpedoed by the United States against the wishes of most members, the assembly intends to adopt a second resolution commending his accomplishments.
Annan, 58, won the unanimous support of the Security Council last Friday after France relented in its threat to veto him, following a week of ballotting against three other African candidates.

In the end France withdrew its objections, mainly because Annan was the clear favourite among the candidates. France was angered by the U.S. veto of Boutros-Ghali and opposition to nominees from French-speaking African countries.
The 185-member assembly must endorse the council's decision.
The plain-spoken urbane Annan, the undersecretary-general for peacekeeping operations, said he invited his opponents to attend the General Assembly events.
Both Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy and Niger's Hamid Algabid, the secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference, were expected to attend.
His other opponent was Ahmedou Ould-Abdallah of Mauritania, a former U.N. envoy for Burundi now based in Washington.

Annan will become the seventh secretary-general of the United Nations since its creation in 1945, the first from sub-Sahara Africa and the only one to have spent his career in the U.N. system, where he was often given dfficult assignments and risky diplomatic missions.

But he faces an organisation under fire from the United States for not reforming its staff and operations quickly enough, a task made more difficult by the $1.3 billion debt owed by Washington that has nearly bankrupted the world body.
He has already said he would speak to Congress if that it was what it took to convince legislators to pay up.

"I think it will be necessary and I am prepared to do so," he said in answer to questions on Monday on the Newshour With Jim Lehrer, adding that "without a stable financial base, it is extremely difficult to carry on reform."
In contrast to Boutros-Ghali, Annan has held a series of administrative jobs, including personnel director, head of budget and finance and programme planning before joining the peacekeeping staff.

Boutros-Ghali, 74, a law professor, author and former Egyptian deputy prime minister, had a long career in international diplomacy, particularly in Middle East. He was a key negotiator of the Camp David talks that led to the 1979 peace treaty between Egypt and Israel.
Watched with interest over the next two weeks will be who Annan will name to his staff, whether any new positions will be created and whether his supporters will be rewarded.

One key official has already given notice. U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa, a veteran journalist and the only woman ever to serve as top speaker for the world body, said on Monday she was leaving at the end of the month.
Foa, who had been on a one-year loan from the U.N High Commission for Refugees, said she would write a book or "try something new in my life."
